Compute ROC Data for Lineup Identification

Source: R/roc_functions.R
make_rocdata.Rd

Computes Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) data from lineup identification experiments following the methodology of Mickes, Wixted, and Gronlund.

Usage

make_rocdata(
  data,
  lineup_size = 6,
  innocent_suspect = "auto",
  thresholds = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A dataframe with the following columns:

  • target_present: Logical. TRUE if guilty suspect in lineup, FALSE if innocent

  • identification: Character. "suspect", "filler", or "reject"

  • confidence: Numeric. Confidence rating (higher = more confident)

lineup_size

Integer. Number of people in the lineup (default = 6). Used to estimate false ID rate when fillers are chosen from target-absent lineups.

innocent_suspect

How innocent-suspect identifications in target-absent lineups are obtained. "designated": the lineups had a designated innocent suspect, so target-absent "suspect" rows are counted directly, and zero such rows means a false-ID rate of zero. "estimated": there was no designated innocent suspect, so the innocent-suspect count is estimated as filler IDs divided by lineup_size. "auto" (the default) chooses "designated" when any target-absent row is a suspect ID or the data have a non-missing suspect_pos column, and "estimated" otherwise, with a message.

thresholds

Optional numeric vector of confidence criteria at which to evaluate the ROC. The default uses the confidence levels of the responses that can move an operating point; see Details. Supplying the criteria of a full sample keeps them fixed across bootstrap resamples.

Value

A list containing:

  • roc_data: Dataframe with correct_id_rate, false_id_rate, and confidence

  • pauc: Partial area under the curve

  • n_target_present: Number of target-present lineups

  • n_target_absent: Number of target-absent lineups

  • thresholds: The confidence criteria used, highest first

Details

This function computes ROC curves following Wixted & Mickes (2012) and Mickes (2015). For each confidence criterion:

  • Correct ID rate = proportion of target-present lineups where suspect identified

  • False ID rate = proportion of target-absent lineups where suspect identified

The criteria are the confidence levels of the responses that enter the ROC: target-present suspect IDs, and target-absent suspect IDs (designated suspect) or filler IDs (estimated). The confidence given to rejections, or to filler IDs in target-present lineups, does not define a criterion, because it cannot move an operating point. Each criterion therefore gives a distinct point, and averages over points (DPP, z-ROC d') do not depend on how rejection confidence was coded.

With a designated innocent suspect, target-absent "suspect" responses are used directly. Without one, filler IDs are divided by lineup size. The two estimators are never added together. See innocent_suspect for how the design is determined.

References

Wixted, J. T., & Mickes, L. (2012). The field of eyewitness memory should abandon probative value and embrace receiver operating characteristic analysis. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 7(3), 275-278.

Mickes, L. (2015). Receiver operating characteristic analysis and confidence-accuracy characteristic analysis in investigations of system variables and estimator variables that affect eyewitness memory. Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition, 4(2), 93-102.

Gronlund, S. D., Wixted, J. T., & Mickes, L. (2014). Evaluating eyewitness identification procedures using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Current Directions in Psychological Science, 23(1), 3-10.

Examples

data(lineup_example)
roc <- make_rocdata(lineup_example)
roc$roc_data
